ABSTRACT

Elections in collegiate and university environments represent the foundational pillar of student participatory democracy, shaping campus governance, student welfare policies, academic representation, and resource allocations. However, traditional collegiate election mechanisms—predominantly relying on manual paper balloting or rudimentary electronic survey portals—suffer from grave structural limitations, including vulnerability to physical and database ballot stuffing, privacy breaches, protracted tabulation delays, a total absence of individual voter verifiability, and severe voter apathy driven by superficial campaign promises lacking empirical scrutiny.

To definitively resolve these challenges, this project presents the Smart & Secure College Voting System (Project No. 94), an enterprise-grade, privacy-preserving, and tamper-evident digital election platform engineered specifically for collegiate institutions. The proposed architecture uniquely integrates two transformative paradigms: (i) an algorithmic Smart Candidate Comparison Matrix & AI Manifesto Engine, which evaluates contesting candidates side-by-side across eight standardized institutional benchmarks with automated feasibility grading and natural-language manifesto querying; and (ii) an immutable, cryptographic Tamper-Evident Merkle Blockchain Ledger Explorer, which ensures verifiable election integrity without compromising voter privacy through strict Zero-Knowledge Decoupling.

Voter identity is verified through a rigorous multi-tier pipeline combining institutional Roll Number roster validation, 6-digit cryptographic SMS OTP authentication, contactless QR badge scanning, and a WebCam Biometric Liveness HUD. Upon authentication, the voter's identity verification state is permanently decoupled from their cast ballot token. The system computes a tamper-proof HMAC-SHA256 digital vote receipt that enables students to independently audit the public blockchain ledger without revealing their selected candidate choice, alongside constitutional NOTA ('None Of The Above') protest safeguards and campus-wide priority polling.

The backend architecture, implemented as an asynchronous RESTful Python service, features an interactive Database Tamper Injection Simulator that dynamically demonstrates how single-bit data modifications violate cryptographic hash chaining and sever the Merkle root, instantaneously flagging unauthorized alterations. To validate scalability, an integrated high-concurrency simulation engine executed 1,000 automated ballot casts across multi-department voter rosters, sustaining a peak throughput of 94.5 transactions per second with sub-60 millisecond latency. Comprehensive environmental lifecycle assessments demonstrate that transitioning a campus election of 10,000 students to this platform eliminates approximately 30,000 sheets of paper, abates 270 kg of CO2-equivalent emissions, and conserves 300,000 liters of water, substantiating the platform's technological robustness, cryptographic security, and ecological sustainability.

CHAPTER-1: INTRODUCTION

1.1 INTRODUCTION & CONTEXT

Elections in higher education institutions constitute the fundamental democratic mechanism through which student bodies exercise self-governance, voice collective grievances, and select representatives to university administrative boards, academic senates, and student activity councils. In modern colleges and technical universities with multi-thousand student populations spread across diverse engineering disciplines, collegiate elections simulate national democratic processes on a microcosm scale. Representatives elected to student councils preside over substantial student welfare budgets, coordinate campus placements, organize national technical symposia, liaise with university leadership on curriculum improvements, and arbitrate student grievances. Consequently, the legitimacy, transparency, and integrity of collegiate electoral outcomes are of paramount institutional importance.

1.2 BACKGROUND & MOTIVATION

The motivation for engineering the Smart & Secure College Voting System arises from acute shortcomings observed across existing university electoral processes: administrative overhead, paper delays, centralized database vulnerabilities, absence of verifiable receipts, and voter apathy.

1.3 PROBLEM STATEMENT

“How to engineer an accessible, web-based digital voting ecosystem for collegiate institutions that enforces strict one-student-one-vote atomicity through multi-factor authentication, guarantees absolute voter anonymity through zero-knowledge identity decoupling, provides mathematical tamper-evidence through a chained Merkle blockchain ledger, empowers students through an algorithmic 8-benchmark candidate comparison matrix with AI manifesto feasibility scoring, and enables independent public receipt verification without introducing coercion vulnerabilities or computational overhead.”

1.4 OBJECTIVES OF THE PROJECT

  • 1. Candidate Matrix & AI Manifesto Engine: 8-benchmark comparative grid with 3-point feasibility scoring and NLP query assistant.
  • 2. Tamper-Evident Merkle Blockchain Ledger: Chained SHA-256 blocks with Merkle roots and real-time database tamper simulator.
  • 3. Zero-Knowledge Decoupling: Absolute voter anonymity with decoupled voter eligibility and anonymous ballot tokens.
  • 4. Multi-Factor & Biometric Liveness HUD: Roster verification, 6-digit SMS OTP, QR identity badge, and WebCam facial liveness detection.
  • 5. Digital Receipt & Public Ledger Verifier: HMAC-SHA256 receipt hash and public audit endpoint.
  • 6. Turnout Analytics & Admin Sentinel: Chart.js analytics across departments and security audit logs.
  • 7. Concurrency Simulation: 1,000-voter high-concurrency simulation and automated Gazette Tabulation Ceremony.
